### Is there an already existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Expected behavior

Multiple independent Windows processes should be able to create and delete DDS participants in the same domain using default participant QoS without assertions or crashes.

Each process in the reproducer creates and deletes participants sequentially. Concurrent participant creation occurs across processes, not across application threads within a process.

### Current behavior

With four concurrent processes using default transports, participant creation intermittently aborts with:

> Assertion failed: open_or_created &&
winapi::get_last_error() != winapi::error_already_exists,
file D:\_fdds\52aab079\Source\fastdds\thirdparty\boost\include\boost/interprocess/sync/windows/semaphore.hpp,
line 65


In one local batch:
- Two processes terminated with exit code 3 after this assertion.
- One process completed all 100 create/delete cycles.

Control runs passed:
- Four concurrent processes with FASTDDS_BUILTIN_TRANSPORTS=UDPv4: all 400 cycles completed.
- One process with default transports: all 100 cycles completed.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Build the following program against the Windows Debug Fast DDS 3.6.2 shared library.
2. Leave FASTDDS_BUILTIN_TRANSPORTS unset.
3. Start four copies concurrently and collect each process’s output.
4. Repeat if necessary; the failure is intermittent.
5. As a control, repeat with FASTDDS_BUILTIN_TRANSPORTS=UDPv4.

```
#include <fastdds/dds/domain/DomainParticipant.hpp>
#include <fastdds/dds/domain/DomainParticipantFactory.hpp>
#include <fastdds/dds/domain/qos/DomainParticipantQos.hpp>
#include <cstdio>

int main()
{
    using namespace eprosima::fastdds::dds;
    auto* factory = DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance();

    for (int iteration = 0; iteration < 100; ++iteration)
    {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "iteration=%d creating\n", iteration);
        auto* participant =
            factory->create_participant(3, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
        if (participant == nullptr)
        {
            return 2;
        }

        std::fprintf(stderr, "iteration=%d created\n", iteration);
        if (factory->delete_participant(participant) != RETCODE_OK)
        {
            return 4;
        }
    }
}
```
The failing path appears associated with Windows shared-memory initialization: the equivalent four-process UDPv4-only control completed successfully. 


The tested standalone probe also configured CRT assertion reporting to stderr and disabled crash dialogs. Those diagnostic settings are omitted above; attach the actual probe source and runner from %TEMP%.




### Fast DDS version/commit

Fast DDS: 3.6.2
Fast CDR DLL file version: 2.3.6

Local build: Windows Debug shared libraries


### Platform/Architecture

Other. Please specify in Additional context section.

### Transport layer

Default configuration, UDPv4 & SHM

### Additional context

Windows, x86-64
MSVC Debug runtime (/MDd)
Standalone reproducer compiler: MSVC 14.51.36260.0

A possible cause is a Windows synchronization-object name collision: the vendored Boost implementation constructs synchronization names using a QueryPerformanceCounter value. However, no matching cross-process semaphore creation trace has been captured, so this remains a hypothesis.

```xml

```

### Relevant log output

```shell

pid=94848 iteration=38 creating
Assertion failed: open_or_created && winapi::get_last_error() != winapi::error_already_exists, file D:\_fdds\52aab079\Source\fastdds\thirdparty\boost\include\boost/interprocess/sync/windows/semaphore.hpp, line 65

pid=46108 iteration=2 created
```

new_candidates.body:
### Intro

Hi!

I am a graduate student at The University of Tokyo, I use MuJoCo skins to render a deformable uterus around the infant.

### My setup

MuJoCo 3.16.0, installed from PyPI (mujoco==3.16.0)
Python API, Python 3.13
Studio launched as python -m mujoco.experimental.studio.viewer
x86_64, Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS


### What's happening? What did you expect?

Studio exits while loading a skin whose vertices are shared by more than one face. The process prints Index count does not match config. and aborts. I expected the skin to render, with vertex normals averaged across the faces that share each vertex.

simulate from the same 3.16.0 release opens this model and draws the skin.

CreateSkinMesh in src/render/filament/support/mesh_util.cc allocates the index buffer with skin_vertnum (PrepareMeshData sets max_indices to the vertex count) and then uploads 3 * skin_facenum indices. Mesh::UpdateIndexBuffer requires those two counts to be equal, so any skin with shared vertices aborts before FillSkinVertices can run. That function already accumulates face normals onto shared vertices.

For the model below, skin_vertnum is 4 and 3 * skin_facenum is 12.

### Steps for reproduction

1. Install mujoco==3.16.0 from PyPI.
2. Save the model below as skin_shared_vertices.xml.
3. Run python -m mujoco.experimental.studio.viewer --model=skin_shared_vertices.xml.
4. The process aborts with Index count does not match config.
5. The same file stays open in simulate.

### Minimal model for reproduction

<details>
<summary>minimal XML</summary>

```XML

<mujoco model="shared skin vertices">
  <visual>
    <headlight ambient="0.4 0.4 0.4" diffuse="0.7 0.7 0.7" specular="0.1 0.1 0.1"/>
  </visual>

  <worldbody>
    <light pos="0 -1 1" dir="0 1 -1"/>
    <geom type="plane" size="1 1 0.01" rgba="0.85 0.85 0.85 1"/>
  </worldbody>

  <deformable>
    <skin name="shared" rgba="0.93 0.55 0.51 1" inflate="0.01"
          vertex="0.15 0.15 0.05
                  0.15 -0.15 0.05
                  -0.15 0 0.05
                  0 0 0.3"
          face="0 1 2
                0 3 1
                1 3 2
                2 3 0">
      <bone body="world" bindpos="0 0 0" bindquat="1 0 0 0"
            vertid="0 1 2 3" vertweight="1 1 1 1"/>
    </skin>
  </deformable>
</mujoco>

```
</details>


### Code required for reproduction

python -m mujoco.experimental.studio.viewer --model=skin_shared_vertices.xml

### Confirmations

- [x] I searched the [latest documentation](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/latest/overview.html) thoroughly before posting.
- [x] I searched previous [Issues](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/issues) and [Discussions](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/discussions), I am certain this has not been raised before.
